in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'd like to claim for my son Alex. He's just turned 18.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

Since Alex is 18 years old, I need to ask a few more questions to determine your eligibility. For children aged 16-19, Child Benefit can usually continue if they remain in approved education or training.

Is Alex currently in approved education or training? This would include things like:
- A-levels or equivalent
- Scottish Highers
- NVQs up to Level 3
- A course at a school or college (but not higher education like a university degree)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any education or training at the moment. He finished school and isn't studying anything right now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. Since Alex is 18 and not in approved education or training, I have a couple more questions:

1. Has Alex recently (within the last 20 weeks) left education or training and registered with either a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services?

2. Is Alex currently working 24 hours or more per week, or receiving any benefits in his own right (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't registered with any careers service or the armed forces. And he's not working - he just helps out around the house really. He doesn't get any benefits in his own name either.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing those details.

I have just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

1. Do you live in the UK?

2. Does Alex live with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - here in Manchester. And yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for all that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Unfortunately, based on what you've told me, I need to share some disappointing news.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

**For Alex (age 18):**
- While you meet the basic requirements (you live in the UK and Alex lives with you), Child Benefit for children aged 16 or over can only continue if they remain in **approved education or training** until they turn 20.
- Since Alex is 18 and is not currently in approved education or training, you would not qualify for Child Benefit for him.
- The provision that allows Child Benefit to continue for 20 weeks after registering with a careers service or armed services only applies to 16 and 17 year olds, so this wouldn't help in Alex's case.

**What could change this:**
If Alex were to return to approved education or training (such as A-levels, NVQs up to Level 3, or other qualifying courses at a school or college), you may be able to claim Child Benefit again until he turns 20. If this happens, you would need to make a new claim.

I'm sorry I couldn't bring you better news. Is there anything else I can help you with?

Since Alex is 18, not in approved education or training, and doesn't qualify for any of the exceptions that would extend eligibility, the claimant is not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.
